subject: Acme POC — Eval plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme POC — Eval plan & success criteria

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared alignment before we draft the POC scope: 

Call recap
- Primary use case: contextual answers for customer support KB (short responses, <200 tokens)
- Expected volume: ~2k queries/day to start, spike to ~10k during promotions
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for inferred online path (hosted/dedicated)
- Data: support KB + recent tickets (no PII in test set)

Success criteria (please confirm):
1) Precision: At least 85% of answers rated 'accurate' by Acme SMEs on a 3-point rubric
2) Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 95% of test queries in dedicated staging
3) Regression: no more than 5% drop in answer quality vs current baseline
4) Cost: projected cost per 1k queries under $X (we'll provide estimate after model selection)

Proposed POC timeline
- Week 0 (this week): finalize evaluation rubric and data slices (you own SMEs, we own infra)
- Week 1: Redwood ships seeded model + eval harness (offline evals)
- Week 2: Shadowing in staging with live traffic split (online shadow)
- Week 3: Joint review and decision / next steps

Ownership
- Acme: provide labeled evaluation set (50–200 queries per critical intent), SMEs for grading
- Redwood: provide POC environment, instrumentation, and evaluation harness; weekly sync cadence

Next steps
1) Can you confirm success criteria above and who from Acme will be the SME graders?
2) Confirm whether Acme is ok with a shadowing stage (we will route a copy of traffic to staging; no external responses sent)
3) We'll attach a draft POC plan after we get your confirmation.

Attachment: acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf (draft POC plan — 3 pages)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.com>

Date: 2027-04-12T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC — Eval plan & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. Confirming the success criteria with a few clarifications: 

- Precision: 85% "accurate" sounds right. Our SME team: me and Bob will do initial grading; I'll loop in 2 additional SMEs once we have >200 items.
- Latency: 350ms p95 is preferable; if that isn't feasible we can consider a staged SLO (first target p95 < 500ms in week 2, optimization sprint in week 3).
- Regression: agreed on <=5% drop.
- Cost: we need a rough estimate to present to procurement — can we get a $/1k queries number by EOW?

On shadowing: yes, we're OK with a staging shadow run as long as no customer-facing responses are served and traffic is anonymized. We'll coordinate with security to sign off on the exact logs to share.

SME grading: I'll be primary grader for the initial set. Bob will help with intent coverage.

Next: please share the POC doc + proposed eval rubric and we'll review.

Regards,
Alice Johnson
Head of Product Ops, Acme Corp
alice@acme.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme POC — Eval plan & success criteria

Hi Alice — great, thanks for the quick confirmation. Per request, attaching the draft POC plan and a starter eval rubric (inline summary below). We'll aim to get a cost estimate by Friday after we size the model options.

Attachment: acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf (draft)

Eval rubric — suggested 3-point scale (Accurate / Partially accurate / Incorrect) with binary pass if Accurate. Key slices to grade: 
- Common intents (50 items)
- Rare intents (30 items)
- Long-context answers (20 items)
- Ambiguous queries (20 items)

Offline vs online: recommendation
- Week 1: offline evals using the labeled set (fast turn-around; catches obvious regressions)
- Week 2: online shadowing in staging with sampled live traffic (validates latency, distribution shift, and real-world coverage)

Instrumentation we will provide:
- Per-query latency, model variant, token counts
- Per-query hash (anonymized) and routing metadata
- SME-only grading UI (we'll share links)

Proposed timeline (re-iterated):
- Apr 13: finalize rubric and data drop
- Apr 16: Redwood delivers seeded model + offline evals
- Apr 20–23: shadowing in staging (sampling 5–10% of traffic)
- Apr 26: joint results review and decision

Can you confirm the rubric slices above and whether Acme wants binary pass/fail or a weighted score for decisioning?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme.com>, Bob Lee <bob.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC — Eval plan & success criteria

Hi all — quick note on grading and evaluation methodology from the Evals team perspective. Appreciate the preference for a simple 3-point rubric. A couple of practical suggestions to make the offline -> online comparison meaningful: 

1) Grading instructions (SME guidance doc) — ask SMEs to judge correctness relative to the KB ground truth and mark "not applicable" if query requires private context not in the POC data. This reduces noise from out-of-scope items.
2) Sampling parity — ensure the offline labeled set mirrors the distribution we'll sample in shadow (intent mix and length buckets). If you can provide a recent week's query logs (anonymized) we'll produce sampling buckets.
3) Weighted decision score — recommend weighted score for go/no-go: 50% Accuracy (SME pass rate), 25% Latency (normalized p95), 25% Coverage (percentage of intents meeting per-intent accuracy threshold). This helps trade off small latency misses vs big accuracy regressions.

On privacy/logging: we'll provide an anonymized hash-only trace and redact any ticket identifiers. Please share security contact for a short checklist — we'll need their sign-off before shadowing.

If you're happy with the weighted scoring approach we'll add the scoring formula to the POC doc and run the offline evals with that metric.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Manager, Evals & Model QA, Redwood Inference
rachel@redwood.com
